evidenceScope: Declarative acceptance specification only; no Catalog/Pricing business implementation, real database/broker/browser execution, accepted contract release or finance readiness is asserted.
notes: Current main is an audit observation, not a published BASE_W02. Source writes depend on the verified wave barrier and bootstrap lease release.
All monetary, quantity, rounding, expiry, replay and timeout boundaries are parameters from explicit accepted policy revisions; no numerical production defaults or prices are supplied here.
Any component fixtures must remain labeled isolated test configuration. They never become production fallbacks or close real provider/consumer integration.
Given/when/then describe future required observations. Every case is NOT_RUN_SPECIFICATION_ONLY and runtimeExecuted=false.
Broker cases apply when accepted event surfaces are enabled; their pending producer/client/ACL prerequisites remain visible rather than being counted as passing or silently skipped.
Account, guest and admin-on-behalf authorization use accepted real Identity contracts. Role names and forwarded headers alone establish no new privilege.
Global CI/infra/contracts/manifests remain E-owned; actual customer/admin consumers remain A/D-owned. This file changes no other owner's source.
No failed, cancelled, missing or skipped required acceptance case counts as success; provider-only evidence keeps the parent INTEGRATION_PENDING.

cases.title: Fresh database and W01 upgrade preserve schema history

E has provisioned distinct disposable service databases and migration identities.
when: Deploy migrations into a fresh database and separately upgrade an existing W01 ServiceMarker database with retained marker data.
Replay migrate deploy and compare the actual migrated schema with the committed service-local schema.
then: Each database reaches the candidate schema with no drift and no cross-owner objects; existing migration checksums and retained rows remain unchanged.
A repeat deploy performs no unintended data change; schema mirrors, new migration IDs and applied history match the candidate.
requiredEvidence: real PostgreSQL fresh and W01-upgrade migration records, checksums and schema diff
candidate SHA/tree, owned migration identities and retained-data comparison

when: Attempt duplicate revision or scoped receipt identity, invalid owned references, invalid time ordering and invalid canonical stored money under the accepted constraints.
Attempt mutation of immutable historical versions through the actual authorized service command paths.
then: Declared database uniqueness and consistency constraints reject invalid writes without partial effects.
Historical snapshot rows remain unchanged; cross-service revision evidence is validated through contracts, without foreign-database joins.
requiredEvidence: real PostgreSQL constraint failures and transaction outcomes
authorized HTTP attempts with before/after immutable row evidence

cases.title: Runtime and migration identities remain isolated

when: Perform ordinary owned DML and attempt runtime DDL, migration-history access, role escalation and connections to another service database.

then: Owned DML works while unauthorized DDL/history/role/cross-database access is denied by PostgreSQL.
No shared database or another run's resource is used or altered; cleanup is limited to resources created by this invocation.
requiredEvidence: real PostgreSQL privilege and connection denial results
E allocation and provisioned database/role/container inventory plus scoped cleanup log

cases.title: Catalog publication is versioned, audited and concurrency-safe

The Catalog service uses its own migrated database and a validated current Identity principal.
when: Publish an audited update and concurrently publish two distinct updates against the same expected revision.
Read both the current definition view and the retained prior revision after one accepted update.
then: Only the permitted publication advances the current revision; the competing stale revision returns the accepted conflict outcome with no extra effect.
Actor, command, prior/new revision and accepted audit evidence are durable; historical descriptions and retirement state remain explainable.
requiredEvidence: real Catalog PostgreSQL and authorized HTTP publication/read results
concurrent revision conflict, durable receipt/audit and historical revision comparison

cases.title: Quote survives service restart with its original calculation

when: Stop only the owned Pricing process and restart it against the same isolated database.
Read the quote and replay its original accepted command through the real service after restart.
then: Quote ID, subject binding, item identities/description references, quantities, adjustments, currency/precision, totals, issue time and expiry remain identical.
Replay returns the recorded outcome; no process-memory reconstruction, current-price recalculation or renewed quote lifetime occurs.
requiredEvidence: real PostgreSQL persisted snapshot/receipt before and after restart
owned process handles and authorized HTTP read/replay response comparison

Accepted publication semantics define revision conflicts and how quote issuance selects an authoritative version.
when: Race price publications with the same expected version and race quote issuance with an accepted price change.
Read quotes created before and after the change and then edit current rates again.
then: Each accepted quote captures one coherent Catalog/price/policy revision set and the amounts resolved from that set.
Stale publications conflict durably; prior quote snapshots never change or contain mixed old/new rates.

authorized publication/quote HTTP results with exact independent expected totals

real PostgreSQL uniqueness and exact effect counts across quote/receipt/audit/Outbox

authorized and forbidden HTTP replay/resource-read results

real PostgreSQL receipt and business/audit/Outbox rows before and after each failure

A committed transaction survives response loss and replays its recorded outcome, without a second quote/publication/event.
requiredEvidence: real PostgreSQL transaction rollback and exact multi-table before/after evidence
fault-injection points and authorized HTTP retry/replay results
